evidence: Plan: "If it carries no `outcome`, one is attached with the existing total classifier `failure.classify_llm_failure` (limit exhaustion `UsageLimitExceeded` → FIX_AGENT_DESIGN ...)"

src/rebar/llm/run_failure.py:57-83: `if isinstance(exc, UsageLimitExceeded): ... budget_err = LLMBudgetExhaustedError(...); budget_err.diagnostic = budget_diag; raise budget_err from exc` (no .outcome)
src/rebar/llm/failure.py:260-310 _map: matches pydantic_ai UsageLimitExceeded only; every other type falls to NEEDS_INVESTIGATION

findings.finding: The plan claims limit exhaustion is classed FIX_AGENT_DESIGN because classify_llm_failure maps UsageLimitExceeded to it. But the production runner never lets a raw UsageLimitExceeded reach the agent step. run_failure.interpret_failure catches it and raises LLMBudgetExhaustedError(...) from exc with no .outcome attached. classify_llm_failure has no arm for LLMBudgetExhaustedError and does not follow __cause__ (_unwrap_retry_error only unwraps tenacity.RetryError), so the outcome the plan attaches is NEEDS_INVESTIGATION. The same applies to RunawayToolLoopError and other LLMError subclasses that are re-raised with a diagnostic but no outcome.
findings.location: Approach > Failed and degraded runs (first bullet); Testing > 'Failure class: limit exhaustion → FIX_AGENT_DESIGN'
scenarios: A real agentic review hits its 60-tool-step / 156-iteration budget: the runner raises LLMBudgetExhaustedError, the new path classifies it NEEDS_INVESTIGATION, and the operator is sent to 'inspect the diagnostic' instead of 'fix the agent design'.
A FakeRunner test that raises a raw UsageLimitExceeded passes and pins behaviour production never shows.
findings.suggested_fix: When last_error has no outcome, classify `last_error.__cause__` if it is set (or add an LLMBudgetExhaustedError → FIX_AGENT_DESIGN arm), and change the limit-exhaustion test so the FakeRunner raises LLMBudgetExhaustedError(...) from UsageLimitExceeded(...), as interpret_failure does.

findings.finding: The plan says a current agentic-signed attestation always has a matching agentic sidecar 'unless `emit_sidecar=False` or pruning removed it'. That list is incomplete. _run_plan_review signs (_finalize_signature) before it calls sidecar.emit, and sidecar.emit is best-effort: it returns False on SecretScreenRefused or any other exception. A failed emit therefore also leaves a signed agentic PASS with no agentic sidecar. The new agentic_review_on_material guard would then be False, and pipeline idempotent_reuse/drift_refresh would reuse or re-sign that agentic PASS until foliated-oceangoing-parrot lands.
findings.location: Approach > Reuse shortcuts stay engine-matched
scenarios: An agentic PASS signs, its sidecar write is refused by the secret screen, and a later pipeline review of the unchanged plan returns idempotent_skip on the agentic attestation.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to: "unless `emit_sidecar=False`, the best-effort emit failed after signing, or pruning removed it", and leave closing the gap to [rebar:foliated-oceangoing-parrot].

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the coverage cause flags (and `model`/`llm_ran`) for a degraded agentic verdict when a scripted step fails rather than the agent call, so a local op fault is not recorded as `llm_unavailable`.
evidence: Plan: "If no agent call failed (a scripted agentic step did), an `LLMUnavailableError` of the step error carrying `classify_llm_failure(None)` is passed."
failure.py:411-420 degrade_cause_flags: any error that is not an LLMInputRejectedError → {"llm_unavailable": True, "input_rejected": False}.
plan_review_recovery.py:340-369 keeps local faults off the outage path: `_config_fault_plan_review_verdict` 'Fail closed for a local criteria/config fault without claiming an LLM outage'.
plan_review_recovery.py:388-404: degraded coverage hardcodes `llm_ran: False` and passes `model=cfg.model`.
findings.finding: The fallback for a failed scripted agentic step (e.g. `plan_review_agentic_inputs` or the new adapter op raising) wraps the error in an `LLMUnavailableError`. `_degraded_plan_review_verdict` passes any non-LLMInputRejectedError through `degrade_cause_flags`, which sets `llm_unavailable: True`. A deterministic local op failure would therefore be recorded as a provider outage, which is the misattribution the pipeline's separate `_config_fault_plan_review_verdict` path exists to prevent. The plan does not say whether this is intended or how to keep the cause flags honest. The degraded path also records `model=cfg.model` (the gate's configured model, not the frontier class) and `llm_ran: False`, even when the agent call ran and then failed. The plan pins the frontier `model` only for the adapted verdict.
findings.location: Approach › Failed and degraded runs (first bullet, 'If no agent call failed (a scripted agentic step did)...')
scenarios: The new adapter raises (e.g. a KeyError while mapping a finding). The verdict says llm_unavailable=True with NEEDS_INVESTIGATION, the operator chases a provider outage, and the real cause is an adapter bug.
The agent call times out after running. The degraded agentic verdict reports llm_ran False and the gate's configured model instead of the frontier model that actually ran.

findings.finding: The degraded-agentic arm changes which disposition surfaces for provider error, timeout, refusal, truncation, limit exhaustion and schema-invalid output. findings.finding: The plan blocks pipeline runs from consuming agentic artefacts only at the three reuse shortcuts. Other pipeline-run readers of the latest REVIEW_RESULT sidecar or signed attestation are not listed, and this change gives them new agentic input. Agentic sidecars will now hold top-level findings with priority 0.7/0.4/0.2 and evidence, and agentic PASSes will sign. Today's interim sidecar holds only the `agentic-adapter-pending` item, so it feeds none of them. The unlisted readers: (a) `sidecar.prior_concerns` (sidecar.py:397-451), the Pass-2 recall that injects prior block/advisory findings with evidence when the material is unchanged. That is exactly the case `agentic_basis` now routes to a full pipeline run. (b) `remediation_mode` eligibility (remediation_mode.py:113, 155) and the rising floor's novelty prior set (`_maybe_apply_rising_floor`, __init__.py:115-123). Both read the latest sidecar and the signed manifest, so an agentic BLOCK or PASS can make a pipeline re-review 'remediation-eligible' and floor pipeline advisories by novelty against agentic findings. (c) `drift_floor.decision` (drift_floor.py:148), which uses a signed attestation as its baseline, and that can now be agentic-signed. The plan says nothing on whether these should also be engine-matched (e.g. skipped when `agentic_basis`) or are intended to cross engines.

The Testing section only checks reuse right after an agentic run and pipeline reuse with no agentic history. No test covers pipeline→pipeline reuse after a pipeline re-review that follows an agentic run.
findings.finding: The engine-matched reuse guard is too broad. `agentic_review_on_material` is True when ANY stored sidecar for the current material has coverage.engine == "agentic". sidecar.all_review_results returns the full retained history, so once any agentic run (a signed PASS, a BLOCK, a degraded INDETERMINATE, or even a DET floor verdict, which the plan also stamps engine=agentic) has a sidecar on material M, idempotent_reuse, verdict_reuse and drift_refresh stay off for every later pipeline review of M. That includes reviews after the pipeline has re-reviewed and signed its own PASS or stored its own BLOCK. The shortcuts actually replay only one record: verdict_reuse and _pass_replay read the latest sidecar (`_latest_reusable_review` → reviews[0]), and idempotent_reuse replays the current attestation.
findings.location: Approach → Reuse shortcuts stay engine-matched (reuse.agentic_review_on_material, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py)
scenarios: An operator tries the agentic engine once, then switches back to pipeline. The pipeline re-reviews and signs a PASS on M, but every later `review-plan` of the unchanged plan runs the full billable four-pass review again instead of reusing it (feature b3e5 regresses), until the plan text changes.

A pipeline PASS is signed on M. One agentic attempt times out (degraded INDETERMINATE, stamped engine=agentic). Back on pipeline, the still-valid pipeline attestation is never reused, and drift_refresh never fires for M.
A pipeline BLOCK is stored after an agentic BLOCK on M. Later pipeline runs never reuse the pipeline BLOCK.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the 'any sidecar' predicate with a check on the specific record each shortcut replays. verdict_reuse already reads `_latest_reusable_review`: skip it when that payload's coverage.engine == "agentic". For idempotent_reuse and drift_refresh, look up the newest sidecar on the current material whose verdict is PASS and that was signed (the one that produced the live attestation), and skip only when that one is agentic. Do not count degraded or DET-floor agentic verdicts as an 'agentic basis'. Add a test: agentic PASS → pipeline review (re-runs, signs) → pipeline review again → idempotent_skip.
